# Agent + Code and Tools

[Home](../../../../README.md) · [All categories](../../../README.md) · [简体中文](in-context-tool-control_cn.md)

Manipulation Action Models → Gripper Manipulation Models → Agent Architectures → Agent + Code and Tools

Agents write programs or call tools to specify motion targets, with IK, trajectory generation and controllers executing them. Record runtime programming, context and experience reuse, feedback and recovery, and whether model weights change. Learned perception alone does not make the action executor a learned policy; retain the historical category code and catalog path.

| [AM.MAN.GRIP.AGENT.ICL.1] <a id="am-man-grip-agent-icl-1"></a> | **GPT-Policy｜Tool calls · In-context learning · Visual feedback**<br>[In-Context Robot Learning with VLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.19138v1)<br>Dongzhou Cheng, Taoran Yi et al<br>**Tags:** `gripper` `bimanual` `agent-architecture` `vlm` `in-context-learning` `tool-use` `video-demonstration` `goal-image` `interaction-history` `execution-feedback` `inverse-kinematics` `real-world` | GPT-Policy organizes demonstration keyframes, optional aligned action records, goal images and interaction history as context for an off-the-shelf VLM with no additional training; the VLM calls tools specifying end-effector poses and gripper commands, a motion execution layer converts these into joint trajectories, and observations and execution results update the context for online adaptation.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Studies five context families: human videos, robot videos with actions, goal images, self-interaction history and online human interaction, across cloth/notebook pickup, bottle opening, plug manipulation, arrangement and mobile exploration. YAM, ARX X5 and Morphi Kino dual-arm gripper configurations are documented, without establishing full task coverage on every platform. Each experimental condition has three trials; some model comparisons are individual runs and task progress is not success rate. VLM weights stay fixed and feedback updates context. Interpolation, IK and time parameterization execute motions; they do not establish collision-free or reliable contact control. | [AM.MAN.GRIP.AGENT.ICL.2] <a id="am-man-grip-agent-icl-2"></a> | **AGP｜Runtime programming · Feedback-driven correction · Experience reuse**<br>[Agent as Policy for Robotic Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.12541v3)<br>Mengzhao Jia, Yang Lin, Xixin Zhang, Zhihan Zhang, Xiaobai Liu, Meng Jiang<br>**Tags:** `gripper` `bimanual` `agent-architecture` `runtime-programming` `code-generation` `tool-use` `task-planning` `execution-feedback` `failure-recovery` `experience-reuse` `persistent-memory` `in-context-learning` `training-free` `video-instruction` `goal-image` `inverse-kinematics` `real-world` | AGP uses a fixed-weight general-purpose agent to write perception and action programs during execution from visual observations, robot state and physical feedback, execute and revise motions through robot interfaces, and save scripts and experience for reuse, enabling closed-loop manipulation without task-specific training.<br>**Evaluation scope:** A preparation agent organizes video/image/language references and interface documentation; the execution agent requests observations, programs geometric estimates and motion targets, and revises actions. Interfaces accept end-effector poses, joint targets and gripper commands; an independent layer handles Mink IK, trajectories and motor feedback. Experience files update context, not weights. Main hardware uses six-joint YAM arms with parallel grippers, including dual-arm folding. Eight configurations cover four-pair assembly, three block structures, dice flipping, throwing and two folding variants. With GPT-6 Astra, seven score at least 80%; simultaneous folding is 3/5. Each has 5 or 10 trials from predefined scenes under time/request budgets. Mean times span 17.71–50.8 minutes, success-only except throwing's all-session accounting, not real-time action generation. P7 + RealHand L6 bottle lifting is qualitative cross-embodiment evidence only. Official resources include code, videos, step observations, joint trajectories and agent traces, not learned action-policy weights. | arXiv v3 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.12541v3) · [Project](https://agent-as-policy-2026.github.io/) · [Code](https://github.com/agent-as-policy-2026/agent-as-policy) · [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Agent-as-Policy/agent-as-policy) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-26 |
| [AM.MAN.GRIP.AGENT.ICL.3] <a id="am-man-grip-agent-icl-3"></a> | **VLCP｜Agent + code control · Within-episode code rewriting · Dual feedback loops**<br>[VLCP: Vision Language Control Policy Closed-Loop Code Replanning for Robot Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.16978v1)<br>Dhia Naouali, Minghan Wu, Claudia Wong, Abhinav Puthran, Omar G. Younis<br>**Tags:** `gripper` `agent-architecture` `coding-agent` `code-as-policy` `runtime-programming` `within-episode-code-rewriting` `execution-feedback` `failure-recovery` `dual-loop-feedback` `multi-view-visual-feedback` `state-delta-conditioning` `jacobian-based-control` `joint-position-control` `persistent-skill-library` `prompt-caching` `training-free` `privileged-object-poses` `franka-panda` `simulation` | VLCP re-queries a frozen VLM every 50 steps to rewrite a control function from before/after images, state changes and execution traces; the function generates joint targets step by step to correct grasping and motion errors within the same episode.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Slow GPT-5.5 reads two RGB views, proprioception, simulator object poses and previous code/action traces to generate control(obs, J). The fast loop reads fresh state and an analytic Jacobian each step, emitting joint-position targets for PD execution. Feedback changes code, not model weights; no RL or demonstration fine-tuning, but prompts include APIs and three control-code examples. MuJoCo/RoboVerse Franka Panda with a parallel gripper runs 57 tasks once each: 10 object picks, 30 kitchen and 17 living-room tasks, with 500-step horizons. Rewriting yields 20/57 (35.1%) versus 2/57 (3.5%) for one-time code generation; the latter still receives per-step state feedback. In additional logs, 15 of 55 episodes containing failed grasps later lift the object (27.3%), not necessarily complete the task. Helpers persist across episodes, but the main comparison resets the library per task and does not establish cumulative transfer gains. Median replanning latency is 18.8 seconds. Real robots, cross-hand transfer and deployment without privileged poses are untested; code/data/weight release is unverified. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.16978v1) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-28 |
| [AM.MAN.GRIP.AGENT.ICL.4] <a id="am-man-grip-agent-icl-4"></a> | **Show-Harness｜Agent + semantic action interface · Deterministic action grounding · Lightweight VLM fine-tuning**<br>[Show-Harness: Just a VLM Agent Can Play Robots](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.10522v1)<br>Yanzhe Chen, Zechen Bai, Zhijun Cao, Wenzheng Zeng, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Yiqi Lin, Guoqiang Liang, Kevin Yuchen Ma, Qiming Huang, Mike Zheng Shou<br>**Tags:** `gripper` `bimanual` `agent-architecture` `vlm` `semantic-action-interface` `discrete-incremental-actions` `deterministic-embodiment-interpreter` `tool-use` `multi-view-visual-feedback` `proprioceptive-feedback` `subtask-planning` `situated-planning` `action-history` `adaptive-step-size` `action-chunking` `failure-recovery` `zero-shot-control` `supervised-fine-tuning` `lora` `gui-demonstration-collection` `gumi` `cross-arm-transfer` `sim-to-real` `franka-research-3` `agilex-piper` `simulation` `real-world` | Show-Harness lets a VLM select discrete semantic micro-actions from images, state and interaction history; embodiment-specific interpreters convert them into pose increments and gripper commands, sharing one interface for frontier zero-shot control, small-model fine-tuning and GUI demonstration collection.<br>**Evaluation scope:** The basic interface has six translations, grasp, release and done, with optional rotations and dual-arm idle. Interpreters supply metric increments, view-to-robot transforms and motion limits; Franka uses impedance control, AgileX IK/joint targets. Zero-shot Gemini-3.1 Pro combines planning/controller roles with subtask checks, history, adaptive steps/chunks and retries. Fine-tuned Qwen3.5-2B predicts action symbols with cross-entropy and rank-64 LoRA, freezing vision/projector, without RL, a dedicated action head or a separate default planner. Deployment feedback changes context/actions, not weights. Real Franka Research 3 (7-DoF) and AgileX (6-DoF, single/dual arm) use parallel grippers; multi-finger hands are untested. Ten standard tasks pair five objects with plate/bowl, normally ten trials each and fifty-step limits. FT jointly trains on both arm platforms using 164 real demonstrations, not unseen-arm zero-shot transfer; separate sim-to-real training uses 230 simulated demonstrations. GUMI records observation/action pairs and low-level traces through the same keyboard/button units. Official releases include code, real/sim data and six LoRA adapters: five real-corpus models and one sim model, requiring their base models. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.10522v1) · [Project](https://showlab.github.io/Show-Harness/) · [Code](https://github.com/showlab/Show-Harness) · [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/showlab/Show-Harness-Data) · [Assets](https://huggingface.co/showlab/Show-Harness-VLMs) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-28 |
| [AM.MAN.GRIP.AGENT.ICL.5] <a id="am-man-grip-agent-icl-5"></a> | **Robo-Harness K1｜Agent + perception tools · 3D measurement and anchors · Tool-call distillation**<br>[Robo-Harness K1: Harnessing Robot-Use Agents via Perception Augmentation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29389v1)<br>Zexi Li, Yehang Zhang, Wenqian Li, Haojian Huang, Chenxu Wang, Shiyuan Deng, Yangkai Wei, Tianyi Zhang, Binghui Xie, Bohan Zhou, Yifan Chang, Kaiwen Zhou, Ying-Cong Chen, James Cheng, Yinchuan Li<br>**Tags:** `gripper` `agent-architecture` `vlm` `tool-use` `perception-augmentation` `rgb-d` `metric-spatial-measurement` `persistent-visual-anchors` `grasp-hypotheses` `execution-feedback` `failure-recovery` `cross-arm-transfer` `bimanual` `tool-call-distillation` `supervised-fine-tuning` `lora` `simulation` `libero-pro` `robosuite` `robotwin` | Robo-Harness K1 packages target segmentation, calibrated depth measurements, anchor tracking and grasp hypotheses as queryable tools; a VLM uses the returned 3D evidence to select motions and gripper commands, while teacher tool-call traces train a smaller model.<br>**Evaluation scope:** The agent reads instructions, RGB, TCP/gripper state and history, emitting one tool name with arguments. SAM3 supplies regions, calibrated depth metric geometry, TAPNext++ tracked anchors and GraspGen grasp hypotheses. Overlays and structured receipts expose evidence without VLM architecture changes or a trained depth encoder; grasp proposals guarantee neither collision-free motion nor success. Perception queries do not advance simulation. Motion tools execute relative displacements, target poses or gripper commands through native controllers, returning actual motion/residuals and fresh images. Frozen frontier models update context and calls, not weights. Qwen3.5-9B freezes vision and uses rank-16 language LoRA to supervise tool calls and short decision notes: 107 successful teacher episodes, 43 conditions and 2,482 filtered targets; no RL or dedicated action head, and deployment still needs tools. All experiments use simulated LIBERO-PRO, RoboSuite and RoboTwin, without real robots. RoboSuite Panda/UR5e/IIWA share PandaGripper, with an attached sponge for wiping: cross-arm transfer, not dexterous-hand validation. Full LIBERO-PRO achieves 139/180 (77.2%). Headline 77.8%/88.9% versus RGB-only 61.1% covers only 18 matched cases and jointly changes perception, memory, motion and completion interfaces, not depth alone. Student results are 19/43 (44.2%) on new states and 5/36 (13.9%) on held-out task conditions, not necessarily new skills. The MIT release provides code, configurations and training interfaces for LIBERO-Pro/RoboSuite; datasets, teacher recordings, trained weights and third-party simulators are not included and require separate inputs/dependencies. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29389v1) · [Project](https://robo-harness.github.io/k1/) · [Code](https://github.com/Robo-Harness/k1) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-29 |
